teaser.text: Aon helps organizations decide which risks to keep, which to insure, and how to support the people who work for them. It makes money mainly from arranging insurance and reinsurance and from advising employers, insurers, and other clients, while much of the cash that passes through it never belongs to Aon.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Aon, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Cash generation, restructuring savings and transaction funding decide the outcome. Aon targets $370 million of cumulative annual savings by year-end 2026 and $450 million of annualized savings by year-end 2027. The Q3 2026 results call is scheduled for October 28. USI is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to regulatory and customary conditions. Client retention and organic growth will test the integration. USI is expected to dilute adjusted EPS in 2027 and add to it in 2028; debt repayment must resume buybacks.

The bear case gives $2,795 million in 2027 and $2,825 million in 2028. It reaches $2,970 million in 2029 because debt, integration costs, weaker pricing, or client losses hold normalized margins below the base case. The bull case gives $3,250 million in 2027 and $3,864 million in 2028. It reaches $4,257 million in 2029 if retention, cross-selling, savings, and deleveraging arrive faster. Aon’s 6% organic growth in both 2024 and 2025 supports continued expansion, but the 2025 disposal gain is excluded from every case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Aon really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations after capital spending. Aon’s own measure is a useful starting point, but it does not represent every dollar available for discretionary use. Stock-based compensation deserves a further deduction because employee awards either dilute existing shareholders or require repurchases to offset that dilution. The resulting figure is a stricter measure of cash available to owners.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Aon today?

paragraphs.text: The earnings multiple needs interpretation. P/E means the share price divided by earnings per share, or how much investors pay for each dollar of profit. Aon’s recent earnings included a gain from selling NFP Wealth, which makes the denominator look stronger than ordinary operations alone. Buybacks can also lift EPS: if the same profit is divided among fewer shares, each remaining share represents more of it. Aon repurchased about $1 billion of shares in 2025, but expects debt repayment to take priority after USI.

blocks.heading: How much does Aon pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise more slowly than the latest increase in the base case. They are $3.41 per share in 2027 and $3.68 in 2028, reaching $3.98 in 2029 through assumed 8% annual increases. The bear case gives $3.28 in 2027 and $3.48 in 2029 after a pause and 3% increases. The bull case gives $3.44 in 2027 and $4.17 in 2029 by repeating 10% increases. Aon raised its quarterly dividend by 10% in 2026 and generated $3,218 million of free cash flow in 2025, supporting increases but not guaranteeing them.

blocks.heading: Does Aon’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Aon’s free cash flow—cash from operations after capital spending—has funded shareholders, acquisitions and debt reduction. A payout above 100% means dividends and buybacks exceeded that cash generation, so borrowing or asset sales filled the gap; a lower payout leaves more cash for the balance sheet.

Cash flow is the practical test of that valuation. Free cash flow means operating cash after capital spending, so it is closer than accounting profit to the money available for debt, dividends and buybacks. Aon generated $3.2 billion of free cash flow in 2025, while first-half 2026 reflected a tax payment tied to the NFP sale and working-capital timing. Its dividend uses only part of the cash, leaving room for other priorities.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management reaffirmed mid-single-digit or greater organic revenue growth and 70–80 basis points of adjusted operating-margin expansion. Its bridge includes 40–50 basis points of operating leverage, 50 basis points from restructuring and a 20-basis-point fiduciary-income drag. It expects strong adjusted EPS growth and double-digit free-cash-flow growth; first-half free cash flow was up 4%.

blocks.heading: What has Aon’s revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: The specialist’s conclusion is measured: Aon’s underlying business is growing broadly, margins are improving and cash remains substantial, but the USI financing and the fading effects of restructuring and disposals will determine how much of that strength is truly recurring.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Aon’s next results?

paragraphs.text: Aon’s Q3 2026 results call is scheduled for October 28. Investors should look for stronger free cash flow, visible restructuring savings and an update on transaction funding. USI is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to regulatory and customary conditions. Closing would begin the integration and deleveraging clock; delay would postpone both the earnings benefit and the operating work.

The practical watchlist is short: Q3 cash generation, Q4 closing, early client-retention evidence, and new disclosures on Vesttoo or tax exposure. Together, those facts will show whether Aon’s larger future is being funded by its business or by still more borrowing.
